title: Grade 5 4.09
description: Learning Outcomes for Grade 5: Represent real-world situations using fractions | Represent fractions from a set | Identify fractions in context | Represent fractions in real-world situations | Represent fractions in practical situations | Solve fraction addition problems | Solve fraction subtraction problems | Simplify fractions in context | Compare fractions in context | Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions | Apply fraction addition in context | Find fractions of quantities | Calculate fractions of quantities | Apply fractions to solve real-world problems

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 8 slices. Emma eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did she eat?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 8.

questions.question: A chocolate bar has 10 pieces. Tom eats 4 pieces. What fraction did he eat?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 10.

questions.question: A class has 20 students. 5 are absent. What fraction is absent?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 20.

questions.question: A tank is divided into 4 equal sections. 1 section is filled. What fraction is filled?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 4.

questions.question: A cake is divided into 6 equal pieces. 2 pieces are eaten. What fraction is eaten?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 6.

questions.question: A ribbon is cut into 5 equal lengths. 3 lengths are used. What fraction is used?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 5.

questions.question: A carton holds 12 eggs. 6 eggs remain. What fraction remains?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 12.

questions.question: A book has 8 chapters. Sarah has read 2 chapters. What fraction has she read?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 8.

questions.question: A tray has 9 muffins. 3 are sold. What fraction is sold?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 9.

questions.question: A garden has 12 plants. 4 are roses. What fraction are roses?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 12.

questions.question: Emma ate 2/8 of a pizza in the afternoon and 3/8 in the evening. What fraction did she eat altogether?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 2 / 8 = 0.25.

questions.question: A tank was 8/10 full. If 3/10 was used, how much remains?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 8 / 10 = 0.8.

questions.question: A class has 24 students. 12 wear hats. What simplified fraction wear hats?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 24.

questions.question: A chocolate bar has 15 pieces. 10 remain. What simplified fraction remains?
questions.solution: Use the key clue in the question and apply the lesson method step by step. This leads to 15.

questions.question: Which is greater: 3/4 of a pizza or 2/3 of a pizza?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 3 / 4 = 0.75.

questions.question: A runner completed 2 1/2 laps. Which improper fraction represents this?
questions.learningOutcome: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 1 / 2 = 0.5.

questions.question: A baker used 3/5 of a bag of flour and later another 1/5. How much was used altogether?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 3 / 5 = 0.6.

questions.question: A school received 120 books. 3/4 were placed in classrooms. How many books were placed in classrooms?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 3 / 4 = 0.75.

questions.question: A farmer harvested 200 apples. 2/5 were sold. How many apples were sold?
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 2 / 5 = 0.4.

questions.question: A water tank holds 300 litres. It is 2/3 full. How many litres of water are in the tank?
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fractions to solve real-world problems
questions.solution: Compute the operation: 2 / 3 = 0.6666666666666666.
